mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions and reduced corporate investment demand.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS change is ≤ 0.25% in all subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 1,000 above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: Over 3 consecutive months with PAYEMS increases > 1,000, the 20-day forward returns remain positive (mean > 0, one-sided t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return turns positive as market anticipates a possible rate hike pause to avoid deflationary pressures.
failure_condition: Over the subsequent 3 months, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior month's (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 5% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening economic momentum and reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive months with INDPRO declines ≥ 5%, the 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (mean ≤ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS (reserves) rises above 500 million dollars, it indicates excess liquidity accumulation, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive 20-day windows with RSAFS 3-mavg > 500, the forward return mean is not significantly greater than zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both unemployment claims (PAYEMS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 500 each suggests conflicting labor-market signals, resulting in a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to heightened uncertainty.
regime_hint: Conflicting labor and price inflation signals
failure_condition: Over 2 consecutive such conflicting months, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (mean ≥ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (not available in the catalog; fallback: use HOUST for manufacturing/demand proxy) below 1,000 units for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as economic activity weakens.
failure_condition: In the following 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (mean > -0.01, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL 3-month moving average falling by ≥ 0.5%) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > previous_month + 0.2%), the S&P 500 60-day forward return turns positive as markets anticipate a rate cut cycle.
regime_hint: Inflation deceleration with labor market loosening
failure_condition: Over 4 consecutive 60-day windows with this regime, the forward return mean is not significantly positive (mean ≤ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).
